newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota chief says weak yen good for its business.
newsitem.headline: Toyota chief says weak yen good for its business.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp president Hiroshi Okuda said on Wednesday that the current weakness of the yen would be more positive for its business than it had expected.
Asked about the dollar's rally to near 123 yen in Tokyo, its highest level in nearly four years, Okuda said : "(That level) would be better for our business than we have expected."
But he added that the company would not change its principle of overseas production, under which it will produce cars in markets where they are purchased.

Asked whether the yen's weakness would boost Toyota's car imports by making them more competitive, Okuda said he didn't think so, but added that exports to other areas, such as the Middle East, where Toyota does not have a production base, may show some increase.

Asked whether he was concerned about Japan-U.S. trade friction because of the current strength of the dollar, he said Toyota's car exports to the United States may show only a marginal increase this year and the company would try to produce cars in the United States as much as possible.
